The binding of Cephaloglycin to Slc22a5, which is a well-documented interaction, supports the hypothesis that Cyclacillin may exert a similar effect, potentially by modulating the activity of Slc22a5. The low common ancestors of Cyclacillin and the beta-lactam antibiotics suggest a shared biological pathway, which may explain the observed interaction.
